messages:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — multiple users reporting high packet loss to customer-facing endpoints in eu-west-1. Alert group: network-egress-high-pktloss. Severity: P1.

mike (sre): seeing same on our end — spikes ~40-60% packet loss to a subset of prefixes via ProviderX. Autoscaling and app health ok but requests timing out to some regions.

zoe (eng-net): confirmed, loss concentrated on routes learned from AS64500 (ProviderX). Route flaps and path divergence to our DNS resolvers as well.

raj (oncall): paging ProviderX NOC now. @providerx-noc can you ack? This is impacting user-facing egress and DNS resolution.

providerx-noc: acked. We see anomalous behavior on our peering cluster in eu-west-1, investigating. Can you share traceroutes and pcap if possible?

mike (sre): attaching traceroute and a short mtr.

mike (sre): ```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.4 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.2 ms  1.3 ms  1.3 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.1  45.6 ms  46.1 ms  45.8 ms
 5  203.0.113.45  46.2 ms  46.3 ms  46.0 ms
```

zoe (eng-net): quick bgp show for the affected prefix: ```
> show ip bgp 203.0.113.0/24
 BGP table version is 456789, local router ID 10.10.0.2
   64500  33434  64512
     via 198.51.100.2 (ProviderX)  valid, external
```

mike (sre): packet captures show ~50% ICMP loss on the egress interface towards ProviderX peer.

providerx-noc: we have correlated control-plane instability on one of our edge routers serving eu-west-1. Our engineers are isolating the linecard. We will update within 15m.

sara (eng): impact assessment — web GET request timeouts for ~18% of users in EU, elevated error rates for API v1 endpoints, and some customers reporting DNS lookup failures for our *.redwood.example hostnames. Marking affected services: api, web, dns-resolvers.

emily (support): currently 6 open tickets citing intermittent 504s and timeouts; customers asking if this is on our side. Sending an acknowledgement note to impacted customers.

raj (oncall): mitigation options? Can we failover away from ProviderX for the most critical prefixes?

zoe (eng-net): we have a backup transit (AS64501) with a partial path to the same prefixes. We can prepend to encourage traffic to move, but risk of transient routing churn. Alternative: announce /24 specific subprefixes via backup transit, or request ProviderX to temporarily move traffic.

mike (sre): preference: short-term announce specific /24s via AS64501 for critical control-plane and DNS prefixes to get immediate relief, then coordinate BGP withdrawal when ProviderX stabilizes.

providerx-noc: we can attempt to steer traffic off the failed linecard to a healthy cluster if you prefer a provider-side mitigation. However, that may take ~5-10m to converge.

sara (eng): which prefixes are highest priority: our authoritative DNS (203.0.113.40/30), API frontends (203.0.113.44/30), and Egress NAT pools (203.0.113.0/24).

zoe (eng-net): preparing route announcements now. Executing controlled announcement of the three critical /24s via AS64501. Will monitor.

mike (sre): command run: ```
# announce via backup transit
bgp announce 203.0.113.0/24 as-path prepend 64501
bgp announce 203.0.113.44/30 as-path prepend 64501
bgp announce 203.0.113.40/30 as-path prepend 64501
```

mike (sre): seeing immediate drop in packet loss to <2% for the announced prefixes. DNS responses for *.redwood.example back to normal for many users. :tada:

providerx-noc: we see reduced traffic on the affected linecard. Our team will continue to drain and replace the unit; ETA 40m for full restoration and BGP stability.

emily (support): updating customers: "We detected provider routing instability affecting connectivity; we've temporarily failed over critical prefixes to a backup transit to restore service. We're continuing to monitor and will provide updates."

raj (oncall): tagging postmortem and incident channel, starting incident doc. @mike please capture timelines, @zoe route decisions, @providerx-noc please provide postmortem when available.

pagerduty-bot: Next on-call rotation window in 1h. Reminder: handoff in thread when handing over.

mike (sre): current status — degraded -> mitigated for critical prefixes. Non-critical bulk egress still sees elevated loss via ProviderX but not customer-impacting for now. Monitoring for 30m.

zoe (eng-net): leaving a comment on routing runbook: prefer provider-side mitigation first unless provider requests customer failover. We'll note that we did customer-initiated failover due to PQ risk to DNS.

providerx-noc: final update: linecard replaced, control-plane stable. We will reintroduce normal path over next 10m unless you prefer to keep backup announcement for a longer soak.

mike (sre): please withdraw backup announcements once you confirm paths stable. Proceed to withdraw in 20m if all good.

providerx-noc: acknowledged. We'll coordinate and post when we see stable MED/AS path for >10m.

mike (sre): withdrawing backup announces now (controlled):``` 
bgp withdraw 203.0.113.0/24
bgp withdraw 203.0.113.44/30
bgp withdraw 203.0.113.40/30
```

mike (sre): monitoring — traffic has returned to ProviderX paths, packet loss remains <1%.

emily (support): sent final customer note: "Connectivity fully restored; cause: upstream provider hardware replacement. We temporarily failed over critical routes to a backup transit to restore service. We will update with a postmortem when available."

raj (oncall): handing over to next oncall @sara in 30m. Leaving incident in watch mode. Please update the incident doc with any provider postmortem.

sara (eng): ack. I'll take the 30m watch and draft the initial incident postmortem.

providerx-noc: post-event note: root cause was a hardware failure on an edge linecard causing control-plane instability and packet forwarding loss to a subset of peers. Maintenance replaced unit at 1990014520. We apologize for the impact.

mike (sre): thanks. Closing real-time mitigation work. We'll capture timelines and RCA in the incident ticket.

incidents-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated, status changed to MONITORING. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0423.

sara (eng): adding action items: (1) add automated detection to escalate provider-level hardware anomalies earlier, (2) refine runbook to prefer provider-side mitigation with timeout thresholds, (3) customer comms templating for provider-caused routing incidents.

mike (sre): noted. Good job triage team. :thumbsup:

raj (oncall): last_message: handing off fully to @sara for post-incident follow-up.
